content.description: A Financial Analyst evaluates a company's financial data, market trends, and investment opportunities to support business decisions. Core work includes building financial models, forecasting revenue and cash flow, valuing assets or deals, and preparing recommendations for management, investors, or lenders. Unlike an Accountant, who focuses on recording transactions and ensuring compliance with accounting standards, a Financial Analyst is forward-looking: the job is about interpreting numbers to answer "what should we do next" rather than "did we record this correctly."

vnMarket.value: In Vietnam, Financial Analyst roles are hired across commercial banks, Big 4 professional services firms, and investment funds/securities companies, with pay and progression differing by employer type. Entry-level analysts typically start around 10-13 million VND/month at Big 4 firms and 11-15 million VND/month at commercial banks, rising quickly with 2-3 years of experience.

salary.value: Fresher/entry-level: 10-15 million VND/month. Analyst (1-3 years): 15-25 million VND/month. Senior Analyst/Assistant Manager (3-5 years): 25-45 million VND/month. International certifications (CFA, ACCA, FRM) can add roughly 20-35% to compensation. Overall average reported for the title is approximately 13.5 million VND/month.

demand.value: Recruitment demand in Banking & Financial Services grew 38.1% year-over-year in Q2 2026, one of the sectors driving hiring growth in Vietnam's job market, alongside a 56.7% YoY jump in Accounting/Auditing demand.

similarJobs.name: Accountant
similarJobs.distinction: Accountant is bookkeeping- and compliance-focused: recording transactions, closing books, and ensuring adherence to accounting standards (VAS/IFRS). Financial Analyst is forecasting-, valuation-, and decision-support-focused: building models and recommending actions based on financial data rather than producing it.

similarJobs.name: Business Analyst
similarJobs.distinction: Business Analyst focuses on process, systems, and requirements analysis across the business; Financial Analyst focuses specifically on financial statements, models, and monetary outcomes.

similarJobs.name: Investment Analyst
similarJobs.distinction: Investment Analyst evaluates securities, portfolios, or deals for external investment decisions (funds, banks); Financial Analyst more often supports internal corporate planning and budgeting, though skill sets overlap.

similarJobs.name: Risk Analyst
similarJobs.distinction: Risk Analyst specializes in identifying and quantifying credit, market, or operational risk exposure; Financial Analyst has a broader remit spanning forecasting, budgeting, and performance analysis, not just risk.

hardSkills.name: Financial modeling
hardSkills.description: Building three-statement models, DCF valuations, and scenario/sensitivity analyses in Excel to project company or project performance.

hardSkills.name: Budgeting & forecasting
hardSkills.description: Preparing and updating revenue, cost, and cash-flow forecasts, and tracking actual-vs-budget variance.

hardSkills.name: Valuation techniques
hardSkills.description: Applying DCF, comparable company, and precedent transaction methods to value businesses, assets, or investment opportunities.

hardSkills.name: Data analysis tools
hardSkills.description: Using Excel (advanced functions, pivot tables), SQL, or BI tools (Power BI/Tableau) to extract and analyze financial and operational data.

hardSkills.name: Accounting & reporting standards literacy
hardSkills.description: Reading and interpreting financial statements prepared under VAS/IFRS well enough to build accurate models, without performing the bookkeeping itself.

softSkills.name: Business partnering
softSkills.description: Working closely with sales, operations, and leadership to translate numbers into decisions, not just deliver reports.

softSkills.name: Communication & presentation
softSkills.description: Explaining complex financial analysis clearly to non-finance stakeholders and senior management.

softSkills.name: Critical thinking
softSkills.description: Questioning assumptions behind forecasts and models rather than accepting inputs at face value.

softSkills.name: Attention to detail
softSkills.description: Catching modeling errors and inconsistencies that could lead to costly misjudgments.

softSkills.name: Time management under deadlines
softSkills.description: Delivering accurate analysis on tight reporting or deal timelines, often for month-end close or live transactions.
